messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: REDWOOD-PAGER-2345 triggered for inference-runtime-high-error-rate in us-west-2 (severity: sev2). Avg 5m error rate 18%. Traces: https://internal.telemetry/redwood/p/2345 :rotating_light:

maya: grabbing this. oncall now. investigating logs + recent deploys.

maya: quick summary from logs: spike started around 12:03 UTC, increased 5xx on /v1/generate path, mostly OOM and connection reset from runtime nodes.

ashwin: i see a tx that shows memory pressure on gpu-node-14, kernel oom messages in dmesg. any recent model swaps or quantization changes?

maya: no model swaps in last 24h per deployment history. there was a config change to batching policy t-2 at 11:50 UTC (by kevin) to increase batch_size to 32 for Llama-weights.

kevin: that change was a small perf tweak to reduce per-token cost, intended for low-latency traffic. rolling back now.

maya: rollback started. patching desired config to batch_size: 16 on canary pool.

ops-bot: Deploy rollback triggered by kevin. Rollback ID: rb-1769954321-a. Status: in_progress.

jess: noted customer impact — a few production tenants reported higher latencies and occasional failures. CS triage Slack thread opened: #customer-impact-2345.

maya: mitigation update: after rollback, error rate dropped from 18% -> 3% in 7m. still seeing intermittent spikes on one host (gpu-node-14).

ashwin: proposal: cordon and restart gpu-node-14, drain pods, reprovision. suspect kernel GPU driver leak under heavy batching.

kevin: +1. scheduling drain now. if restart clears we should add a guard in runbook: never raise batch_size beyond 24 on older driver images.

maya: draining node, moving active sessions to fallback pool.

ops-bot: Node drain initiated: gpu-node-14. Evicting 12 pods.

maya: node restart completed. post-restart checks: driver v470 still present, mem usage normal, no OOMs in dmesg. error rate stable at 0.9%.

jess: good. can we quantify customer impact window for postmortem? CS timeline will need start/end + affected customers.

maya: agreed. tentative impact window 11:50 UTC (config change) -> 12:12 UTC (stable after restart). collecting request ids and tenant ids now.

ashwin: capturing traces and perf counters to S3: s3://redwood-incident-archives/1769954321/traces.tar.gz. includes kernel logs + runtime logs + batch latency histograms.

kevin: created ticket RW-INC-2345 in Jira for follow-up, link: https://jira.internal/redwood/browse/RW-INC-2345. tagging owners for remediation.

jess: scheduling postmortem. can we set a tentative 30-min slot today for async recap + action assignment?

maya: i'm available 16:00 UTC. carol can you chair the postmortem?

carol: yes I can. please add agenda: incident timeline, root cause hypothesis, immediate mitigations, runbook gaps, action items + owners, verification plan.

jess: added calendar invite: "RW-INC-2345 postmortem" 16:00-16:30 UTC. invite link: https://calendar.redwood/meet/pm-1769954321.

maya: quick list of actionable items to track now (assigning owners):
- "Investigate batching regression" -> owner: ashwin, due: 2026-04-10
- "Add guard in runbook for batch_size vs driver version" -> owner: kevin, due: 2026-04-07
- "Customer impact summary + CS outreach" -> owner: jess, due: 2026-04-06
- "Node health automation: auto-restart on persistent GPU OOM" -> owner: carol, due: 2026-04-20

ashwin: noted. i'll start with reproducer on staging with driver v470 and batch_size 32. will attach logs to RW-INC-2345.

kevin: i'll add a small table to the runbook (runbooks/oncall/batching.md) with matrix: driver-version vs safe-batch-size + verification commands. snippet i'll add:```
# verification
kubectl exec -it loadtest -- ./run-batch-check --model LlamaX --batch 32 --seq 1024
```

maya: good call. also add an explicit rollback procedure step referencing ops-bot rollback command and how to validate stability. ran into slight confusion during incident about exact ops-bot syntax.

carol: i'll own the runbook edit review. kevin please give PR by EOD tomorrow. i'll merge after validation.

jess: CS outreach draft: "We experienced elevated errors between 11:50–12:12 UTC due to a batching config change. The issue was mitigated and service is stable. We will follow up with a more detailed postmortem and any customer-specific impact notes." i'll send after postmortem.

maya: one more immediate follow-up: add an automated alert that trips when error rate > 10% AND correlated with config changes in last 15m. could reduce noisy pagering for unrelated issues. owner: ops-alerting team (I've pinged them).

ops-bot: Action created: RW-INC-2345-A1 (Investigate batching regression) assigned to ashwin.

ops-bot: Action created: RW-INC-2345-A2 (Runbook add guard) assigned to kevin.

ops-bot: Action created: RW-INC-2345-A3 (Customer outreach) assigned to jess.

carol: during the postmortem we'll also pick a verification checklist for the runbook change. want a post-change smoke test in staging for at least 24h before lifting constraints.

maya: handoff notes for next oncall (kevin will take shift):
- incident mitigated, rollback in place, node restart done
- error rate stable under 1%
- actions created in Jira RW-INC-2345
- runbook patch PR expected from kevin by EOD tomorrow

kevin: acknowledged, taking handoff. thanks maya.

jess: closing notes: please update the incident thread with any new evidence. we'll link the postmortem doc here after meeting.

maya: thanks team. switching to follow-up mode.

ops-bot: Thread pinned to channel. Incident state: monitoring -> resolved.

carol: postmortem doc draft link (will be populated during meeting): https://docs.internal/redwood/postmortems/RW-INC-2345-draft. please add any notes you want me to include before 15:45 UTC.

maya: adding initial timeline and logs to doc now.

ashwin: i'll add reproducer steps and a short root-cause hypothesis section: "increased batch_size caused memory pressure on nodes running older GPU driver (v470) leading to intermittent OOM and connection resets."

kevin: will open the runbook PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runbooks/pull/1123

jess: thanks everyone. follow-ups will be tracked on RW-INC-2345 and the runbook PR. :white_check_mark:
